input.quote: 5.3 Any of the Parties may at its own expense insure against risks so far as its own share of such costs is concerned. Should the Parties jointly agree to insure against risks, the costs of such insurance shall form part of the Capital Costs, as approved by the Management Committee.
input.rationale: The INSURANCE rule targets a services/hosting vendor that touches our data or premises. This is a multi-party APCN 2 cable construction and maintenance consortium agreement: the counterparties are co-owning carrier Parties (each with mutual, several obligations and pro rata cost-sharing under Schedule B), not a vendor providing services to us or processing Customer Data, and no Party occupies our premises under this Agreement. The Suppliers are engaged under a separate Supply Contract placed by the PG, so any supplier insurance sits in that instrument, not here. The Agreement does address insurance on a mutual basis: Subparagraph 5.3 permits each Party to insure its own share of risk at its own expense and allows joint insurance charged to Capital Costs, Subparagraph 5.1(d) treats insurance (or a reasonable allowance in lieu of self-insured risk) as a recoverable Capital Cost, and Subparagraph 21.2 gives a third-party indemnity capped at each Party's Schedule B share. Because the rule's premise (a vendor relationship) is absent, there is nothing to insert; note also that any inserted coverage mandate would bind us symmetrically as a Party and so would not benefit our side. No coverage limits are specified, which we record in the rationale rather than as a deviation given the mutual consortium structure and the low severity of this rule.
